financials_interim.notes: R I L PROPERTY PLC COMPANY (standalone parent, = the Rental/property-leasing segment) basis, three months ended 30 June 2026. Revenue Rs.474,231k, +24.3% YoY (2025: Rs.381,386k) -- rental and related services only. Gross Profit +25.7% YoY (Rs.337,451k to Rs.424,067k). Administrative Expenses rose 38.6% YoY (Rs.122,656k to Rs.170,009k) -- a real cost increase not offset elsewhere, restraining operating-profit growth to +12.4% (Rs.412,798k to Rs.464,075k) despite the stronger gross-profit growth. PBT +7.1% YoY (Rs.396,645k to Rs.424,668k) -- the smallest-growing of RIL's three operating segments (see GROUP row's notes for the Automobile/Renewable-Energy segment comparison), as Net Finance Expenses more than doubled (Rs.16,153k to Rs.39,407k, +144.0%) and further eroded the operating-profit gain. PAT +6.6% YoY (Rs.395,461k to Rs.421,619k); EPS Rs.0.53 (2025: Rs.0.49). Operating cash flow was NEGATIVE this quarter, Rs.(124,642)k (2025: positive Rs.227,152k) -- a Rs.351,794k swing, driven by a Rs.293,466k increase in Trade and Other Receivables (working-capital build, Cash Flow Statement p.5) against a Rs.18,298k increase in the prior-year comparative -- a genuinely weaker cash-conversion quarter at Company level, worth flagging even though it does not appear in the P&L. short_term_borrowings=640,494 (Interest Bearing Loans and Borrowings, current, 625,200 + Bank Overdrafts 15,294); long_term_borrowings=2,276,464 (non-current Interest Bearing Loans and Borrowings).

Source: R I L PROPERTY PLC Interim Condensed Financial Statements, three months ended 30 June 2026 (filed CSE 13-Aug-2026). FYE 31 March. Income Statement p.2, SOFP p.3, Cash Flow p.5, Note 3 Revenue (disaggregation) p.6, Note 12 Segmental Information p.10. GROUP (consolidated) basis. RIL Property is a diversified holding company: subsidiaries include United Motors Lanka PLC (automobile sales/distribution -- dominant segment) and Panasian Power PLC (renewable energy generation), with the Company itself operating the Rental/property-leasing (Property Leasing) segment. REVENUE MIX (Note 3, p.6): Automobile Sales and Related Services Rs.13,453,284k (91.7% of Group revenue this quarter), Renewable Energy Rs.733,023k (5.0%), Rental and Other Related Services Rs.474,231k (3.2%, =Company), Vehicle Hiring Rs.1,485k (new, immaterial). SEGMENTAL PBT DRIVER (Note 12, p.10): Group PBT grew Rs.889,863k YoY (Rs.688,283k to Rs.1,578,146k, +129.3%), decomposing exactly as: Automobile segment PBT +Rs.687,253k (Rs.448,215k to Rs.1,135,468k, +153.3%) = 77.2% of the Group increase; Renewable Energy segment PBT +Rs.194,166k (Rs.35,451k to Rs.229,617k, +547.6%) = 21.8%; Rental/Company segment PBT +Rs.28,023k (Rs.396,645k to Rs.424,668k, +7.1%) = 3.1%; Inter-segment eliminations worsened by Rs.(19,146)k; Vehicle Hiring immaterial loss of Rs.(433)k. Automobile revenue more than doubled (Rs.6,586,103k to Rs.13,453,284k, +104.3%), accounting for 93.1% of the Group's Rs.7,379,578k total revenue increase (Rs.7,282,445k to Rs.14,662,023k, +101.3%). tax_expense=415,270 vs 111,001 PY (+274.1%, effective rate rose from 16.1% to 26.3%) is not separately explained in the filing, but the segmental tax note (p.10) shows the Renewable Energy segment swinging from a Rs.36,662k tax REVERSAL (credit) in 2025 to a Rs.(77,989)k tax EXPENSE in 2026 -- a Rs.114,651k unfavourable tax swing on its own, alongside Automobile segment tax rising roughly in proportion to its PBT growth (Rs.146,479k to Rs.334,232k, +128.2%); together these are the mechanical source of the higher effective rate, though no qualitative explanation (e.g. tax holiday expiry) is given for the Renewable Energy reversal-to-expense swing -- flagged as a genuine gap. Net Finance (Expenses)/Income WORSENED YoY, from a Rs.(46,594)k net cost to a Rs.(297,837)k net cost (a Rs.251,243k larger drag), as Finance Income fell 37.2% (Rs.232,055k to Rs.145,624k) while Finance Expenses rose 59.2% (Rs.278,649k to Rs.443,461k) -- a genuine headwind that PARTIALLY offset the segmental operating gains at the PBT line (Operating profit alone grew Rs.1,140,364k, +155.1%, more than the Rs.889,863k PBT growth, with the finance-cost deterioration absorbing the difference). NOTABLE: Group PAT +101.4% (Rs.577,282k to Rs.1,162,876k) but EPS grew only +68.6% (Rs.0.51 to Rs.0.86) because Non-Controlling Interest's profit share grew faster than owners' (NCI Rs.167,112k to Rs.478,853k, +186.5%, rising from 28.9% to 41.2% of Group PAT) -- consistent with the Automobile/Renewable-Energy subsidiaries (United Motors Lanka, Panasian Power) not being wholly owned and growing faster than the wholly-owned Rental/Company segment; shares in issue unchanged at 800,000,000 (Note 7, p.7) so no dilution is involved. current_assets/current_liabilities, total_liabilities are printed as single lines on the face of the SOFP and used directly (Total Liabilities = Non-Current 14,193,985 + Current 14,169,705 = 28,363,690, ties to Total Assets 64,198,995 - Total Equity 35,835,305 exactly). short_term_borrowings=7,769,794 (Interest Bearing Loans and Borrowings, current, 7,467,486 + Bank Overdrafts 302,308); long_term_borrowings=6,968,746 (Interest Bearing Loans and Borrowings, non-current). cash_and_equivalents=808,347 is the BS 'Cash and bank' figure; the Cash Flow Statement's closing balance of 506,039 nets off the 302,308 Bank Overdraft (808,347-302,308=506,039 exactly) -- consistent, not a discrepancy. capex=206,412 is 'Acquisition of Property, Plant and Equipment' only; a further Rs.640k on intangible assets and Rs.67,583k on investment property additions are excluded from the capex field (both disclosed separately in the Cash Flow Statement, p.5).

thesis.thesis_text: R I L Property PLC is a diversified holding company (Retailing sector) whose Group results are dominated by its majority-owned Automobile Sales subsidiary, United Motors Lanka PLC, and a smaller Renewable Energy subsidiary, Panasian Power PLC, alongside RIL's own directly-held Rental/property-leasing business. In Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), Group Revenue more than doubled YoY (+101.3% to Rs.14,662,023k) and PAT grew 101.4% to Rs.1,162,876k, with United Motors Lanka alone contributing 93.1% of the Group's revenue increase and 77.2% of its PBT increase. At ~7.0x annualised trailing P/E and ~0.54x P/B with a rising dividend (Rs.1.00 FY2026, up from Rs.0.20 FY2024), the stock looks statistically cheap. However, EPS growth (+68.6%) trailed PAT growth because Non-Controlling Interest's share of Group profit rose from 28.9% to 41.2% YoY, and RIL's own wholly-owned Rental segment posted negative operating cash flow this quarter on a receivables build -- the headline growth is a subsidiary story more than a RIL-specific one (Interim Financial Statements, Note 3 p.6 and Note 12 p.10).
thesis.gaps_note: Macro & Industry Outlook (10% weight) unavailable -- no CBSL/vehicle-import-policy/renewable-energy-tariff data source exists in this project; the remaining five pillars are renormalized to sum to 100% (Financial Quality 33.3%, Growth 22.2%, Valuation 22.2%, Business Quality 16.7%, Governance & Risk 5.6%). Confidence is limited: only ONE interim quarter is on file (no annual report review, no multi-period trend beyond the three-year dividend history), no peer-holding-company comparison exists, and two filing-level gaps (the Renewable Energy tax swing and the finance-cost deterioration) are not qualitatively explained by the company.

financial_quality.rationale: Q1 FY2026/27 (qtr ended 30 June 2026) Group operating margin improved to 12.8% from 10.1% YoY and PAT grew 101.4% to Rs.1,162,876k, but earnings quality is mixed: the effective tax rate jumped from 16.1% to 26.3% (tax expense +274.1% YoY) on an unexplained Renewable Energy segment tax swing, and Net Finance Expenses worsened Rs.251,243k YoY (finance income -37.2%, finance costs +59.2%) as Automobile-segment inventory financing needs grew (Inventory Rs.10,332,937k on the Group balance sheet). Total liabilities/equity of 0.79x (28,363,690/35,835,305) and a current ratio of 1.46x (20,651,163/14,169,705) are moderate, not stretched. At the standalone Company (core Rental) level, operating cash flow was NEGATIVE this quarter, Rs.(124,642)k vs positive Rs.227,152k PY, on a working-capital build in receivables -- a genuine quality flag masked by the Group-level Automobile-driven headline.

growth_outlook.rationale: Group Revenue more than doubled YoY (+101.3%, Rs.7,282,445k to Rs.14,662,023k) and PBT grew 129.3%, but this growth is almost entirely a single-segment story: the Automobile Sales subsidiary (United Motors Lanka PLC) contributed 93.1% of the Group's revenue increase and 77.2% of the PBT increase, with its own revenue more than doubling (+104.3%). The smaller Renewable Energy segment (Panasian Power PLC) grew off a low base (+547.6% PBT), contributing a further 21.8% of the PBT increase. RIL's own core Rental/property-leasing segment (the Company entity) grew a much slower 7.1% at the PBT line -- the headline growth rate is not representative of RIL's own directly-operated business, and depends on vehicle-import volumes/policy at United Motors Lanka, a cyclical, import-regulation-sensitive driver outside RIL's control as a majority-but-not-sole owner.

valuation.rationale: At Rs.24.20 (2026-08-28), trailing-quarter-annualised EPS of Rs.3.44 (Q1 basic EPS Rs.0.86 x4) implies a P/E of ~7.0x, and book value of ~Rs.44.79/share (Group total equity Rs.35,835,305k / 800,000,000 shares, though this includes Non-Controlling Interest and is not owners'-equity-only) implies a P/B of ~0.54x -- statistically cheap on both counts. Dividends have grown from Rs.0.20 (FY2024) to Rs.0.55 (FY2025) to Rs.1.00 (FY2026), a rising trend implying a ~4.1% trailing yield. The cheapness needs some discount for the fact that 41.2% of Group PAT this quarter accrues to Non-Controlling Interest, not RIL's own shareholders, and EPS growth (+68.6%) trailed PAT growth (+101.4%) for exactly this reason.
citations: dividends: FY2026 DPS 1.00, FY2025 DPS 0.55, FY2024 DPS 0.20

business_quality.rationale: RIL Property is a diversified holding company (Retailing sector per coverage universe) rather than a single operating business: its dominant earnings driver, United Motors Lanka PLC (automobile sales/distribution), is a majority-owned but not wholly-owned subsidiary exposed to Sri Lanka's vehicle-import-permit and forex-availability cycle -- a real structural risk for a minority-interest-heavy holding structure, evidenced by NCI's share of Group PAT rising from 28.9% to 41.2% YoY. The smaller Renewable Energy subsidiary (Panasian Power PLC) adds diversification. RIL's own directly-held Rental/property-leasing segment is modest (3.2% of Group revenue) and posted negative operating cash flow this quarter on a receivables build -- the core, wholly-owned business is not currently the platform's growth engine.

governance_risk.rationale: No circulars/disclosures feed exists in this project to independently verify board or ownership changes. The complex multi-subsidiary holding structure (Automobile, Renewable Energy, Property, and a newly-disclosed immaterial Vehicle Hiring segment) is transparently segmented in the filing (Note 12), a positive for disclosure quality, but two items are not qualitatively explained by the company: the Renewable Energy segment's swing from a tax credit to a tax expense (a Rs.114,651k unfavourable move) and the sharp YoY deterioration in net finance costs -- both flagged as genuine filing-level gaps rather than governance red flags per se.

key_reasons: Group PAT grew 101.4% YoY to Rs.1,162,876k on Group revenue more than doubling (+101.3%), driven overwhelmingly (93.1% of the revenue increase, 77.2% of the PBT increase) by the Automobile Sales subsidiary, United Motors Lanka PLC
Statistically cheap at ~7.0x annualised trailing P/E and ~0.54x P/B, with a rising dividend (Rs.0.20 to Rs.0.55 to Rs.1.00 over FY2024-FY2026) implying a ~4.1% yield

Non-Controlling Interest's share of Group PAT rose from 28.9% to 41.2% YoY, meaning EPS growth (+68.6%) trailed PAT growth (+101.4%) -- the per-share number, not the consolidated headline, is the more relevant metric for RIL's own shareholders
watch_factors: Group growth is concentrated in a single, not-wholly-owned Automobile-distribution subsidiary exposed to Sri Lanka's vehicle-import-permit/forex cycle -- a policy-driven risk outside RIL's control

RIL's own core Rental/property-leasing (Company) segment posted NEGATIVE operating cash flow this quarter, Rs.(124,642)k, on a working-capital build in receivables -- worth tracking separately from the subsidiary-driven Group headline

Effective tax rate rose from 16.1% to 26.3% YoY on an unexplained Renewable Energy segment tax swing, and net finance costs worsened by Rs.251,243k YoY -- both real drags not discussed qualitatively by the company

horizon_notes.6m: Next quarterly filing will show whether United Motors Lanka's auto-sales momentum continues or whether the effective tax rate and finance-cost drags persist.
horizon_notes.1y: If NCI's growing share of Group PAT continues, EPS growth will keep trailing headline PAT growth -- worth modelling on a per-share basis rather than the consolidated numbers.
horizon_notes.3y: Thesis depends on Sri Lanka's vehicle-import policy/forex availability remaining supportive for United Motors Lanka, since this single subsidiary now drives the large majority of Group earnings growth.
horizon_notes.5y: No macro/industry data source in this project to assess a multi-year vehicle-import-policy or renewable-energy-tariff cycle that would materially affect RIL's two key subsidiaries.

interim_updates.note_text: R I L Property PLC (RIL) reported Group Revenue of LKR14,662,023k for the quarter ended 30 June 2026, more than doubling YoY, +101.3% (2025: LKR7,282,445k). RIL is a diversified holding structure: Automobile Sales and Related Services (subsidiary United Motors Lanka PLC) contributed LKR13,453,284k, 91.7% of Group revenue this quarter, and MORE THAN DOUBLED YoY (2025: LKR6,586,103k, +104.3%) -- accounting for 93.1% of the Group's total LKR7,379,578k revenue increase (Revenue disaggregation, Note 3, p.6). Renewable Energy (subsidiary Panasian Power PLC) contributed LKR733,023k (5.0% of revenue, +132.7% YoY); Rental and Other Related Services (=Company, property leasing) contributed LKR474,231k (3.2%, +24.3% YoY). By SEGMENT PBT (Note 12, p.10): Automobile segment PBT grew LKR687,253k YoY (LKR448,215k to LKR1,135,468k, +153.3%) = 77.2% of the Group's total LKR889,863k PBT increase; Renewable Energy PBT grew LKR194,166k (LKR35,451k to LKR229,617k, +547.6%) = 21.8%; Rental/Company PBT grew a much smaller LKR28,023k (LKR396,645k to LKR424,668k, +7.1%) = 3.1%. Group Profit from Operating Activities grew even faster than PBT, +155.1% YoY to LKR1,875,647k (2025: LKR735,283k), but Net Finance Expenses WORSENED sharply, from a LKR46,594k net cost to a LKR297,837k net cost (a LKR251,243k larger drag) as Finance Income fell 37.2% YoY (LKR232,055k to LKR145,624k) while Finance Expenses rose 59.2% (LKR278,649k to LKR443,461k) -- this financing-cost deterioration absorbed roughly a fifth of the operating-profit gain before it reached the PBT line. Group PBT grew 129.3% YoY to LKR1,578,146k (2025: LKR688,283k). Income Tax Expense grew a disproportionate +274.1% YoY to LKR415,270k (2025: LKR111,001k; effective rate rose from 16.1% to 26.3%), driven partly by the Renewable Energy segment swinging from a LKR36,662k tax REVERSAL (credit) in 2025 to a LKR(77,989)k tax EXPENSE in 2026 (a LKR114,651k unfavourable swing on its own) alongside Automobile segment tax rising roughly in proportion to its PBT growth -- no qualitative explanation (e.g. tax-holiday expiry) is given for the Renewable Energy swing. Group PAT grew 101.4% YoY to LKR1,162,876k (2025: LKR577,282k), but EPS grew only +68.6% (LKR0.51 to LKR0.86) because Non-Controlling Interest's profit share grew faster than owners' (NCI LKR167,112k to LKR478,853k, +186.5%, rising from 28.9% to 41.2% of Group PAT) -- consistent with United Motors Lanka and/or Panasian Power not being wholly owned; shares in issue unchanged at 800,000,000. At the COMPANY (Rental/property-leasing) level, Revenue grew +24.3% YoY to LKR474,231k, but Administrative Expenses rose 38.6% YoY (LKR122,656k to LKR170,009k), limiting Operating Profit growth to +12.4% and PBT growth to +7.1% (LKR396,645k to LKR424,668k) -- Company operating cash flow was NEGATIVE this quarter, LKR(124,642)k (2025: positive LKR227,152k), on a LKR293,466k working-capital build in Trade and Other Receivables.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: RIL's prior on-file document (nine months ended 31 December 2024, filed Feb-2025) predates this 30 June 2026 quarter by well over a year -- the CSE API confirms RIL has continued filing on schedule since (this quarter filed 13-Aug-2026, within the standard 45-day interim window; annual reports for FY2024/25 and FY2025/26 both on file), so the gap was purely a local sourcing lag, NOT suspension, delisting risk, or non-disclosure. No closer prior quarter has yet been entered into financial_statements/interim_updates to support a QoQ comparison, only this fresh entry. Genuine filing-level gaps: (1) the Renewable Energy segment's swing from a LKR36,662k tax reversal (credit) in 2025 to a LKR(77,989)k tax expense in 2026 is disclosed only as a segmental figure (Note 12, p.10) with no qualitative note explaining the mechanism (e.g. exhaustion of a tax holiday/incentive period typical for renewable-energy generation projects in Sri Lanka is plausible but not confirmed by the filing); (2) the LKR251,243k YoY worsening in Net Finance Expenses (Finance Income -37.2%, Finance Expenses +59.2%) is not explained qualitatively -- plausibly linked to the working-capital-intensive growth of the Automobile segment's import/inventory financing given Inventories of LKR10,332,937k on the Group balance sheet, but this is inference, not disclosed fact; (3) no balance-sheet comparative as at 30 June 2025 is presented (interim SOFPs compare only to the 31 March 2026 FYE), so no YoY balance-sheet metrics could be computed, only YoY income-statement metrics; (4) the Vehicle Hiring and Facility Management segment is newly disclosed this quarter with no prior-year comparative -- treated as immaterial (LKR1,485k revenue, LKR(433)k loss).
interim_updates.takeaway: RIL's headline growth (Group revenue +101.3%, PBT +129.3%, PAT +101.4%) is almost entirely an Automobile-segment (United Motors Lanka) story: that segment alone drove 77.2% of the Group's PBT increase on revenue more than doubling, with the smaller Renewable Energy segment (Panasian Power) contributing a further 21.8% off a much lower base (+547.6%). RIL's own core Rental/property-leasing business (the Company entity) grew a modest 7.1% at the PBT line and actually posted NEGATIVE operating cash flow this quarter on a working-capital build -- worth watching separately from the subsidiary-driven headline numbers. A LKR251,243k YoY worsening in net finance costs and a rising effective tax rate (16.1% to 26.3%, partly from a Renewable Energy tax-credit-to-expense swing) are real, quantified headwinds that mean EPS growth (+68.6%) trailed PAT growth (+101.4%) even before accounting for the growing Non-Controlling Interest share -- for RIL as a minority shareholder in its own operating subsidiaries, the per-share growth rate is the more relevant number to track than the consolidated headline.
operational_highlights: Group Revenue LKR14,662,023k, +101.3% YoY (2025: LKR7,282,445k); Group Profit from Operating Activities LKR1,875,647k, +155.1% YoY; Group PBT LKR1,578,146k, +129.3% YoY; Group PAT LKR1,162,876k, +101.4% YoY.

Automobile Sales segment (United Motors Lanka PLC) revenue more than doubled YoY, LKR6,586,103k to LKR13,453,284k (+104.3%), and its segment PBT grew LKR687,253k (+153.3%) -- 77.2% of the Group's total PBT increase.
Renewable Energy segment (Panasian Power PLC) PBT grew LKR194,166k YoY (+547.6%, LKR35,451k to LKR229,617k) -- 21.8% of the Group's PBT increase, the second-largest contributor.

Net Finance Expenses worsened LKR251,243k YoY (a net cost of LKR46,594k to LKR297,837k) as Finance Income fell 37.2% while Finance Expenses rose 59.2% -- a real headwind that absorbed part of the operating-profit gain before the PBT line.

Effective tax rate rose from 16.1% to 26.3% (Income Tax Expense +274.1% YoY to LKR415,270k), partly driven by the Renewable Energy segment swinging from a LKR36,662k tax credit to a LKR(77,989)k tax expense.
Non-Controlling Interest captured a growing share of Group PAT (28.9% to 41.2%), so EPS grew only +68.6% (LKR0.51 to LKR0.86) versus Group PAT growth of +101.4%.
key_drivers: Automobile segment (United Motors Lanka) PBT growth of LKR687,253k YoY (+153.3%) is the dominant driver, 77.2% of the Group's total PBT increase, on revenue more than doubling.
Renewable Energy segment (Panasian Power) PBT growth of LKR194,166k YoY (+547.6%) is the second-largest driver, 21.8% of the increase.
A LKR251,243k YoY deterioration in Net Finance Expenses (income -37.2%, costs +59.2%) is a genuine drag that prevented PBT growth (+129.3%) from matching the faster operating-profit growth (+155.1%).

Non-Controlling Interest absorbing a growing share of Group PAT (28.9% to 41.2% of PAT) means EPS growth (+68.6%) understates from the owners' perspective relative to the headline Group PAT growth (+101.4%).

_gaps: ebitda: depreciation_amortization not disclosed; EBITDA understated (= operating profit only)
